source.title: Shared Geometry Is Not Shared Physics: A Layerwise Test of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis in Astronomy
source.authors: Kshitij Duraphe; A. Kannappan; Dun-Li Chan; Okiki Famutimi; Yaswant Sai Ejjagiri; Michael J. Smith; John F. Wu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures representational alignment across model scale and depth, and tests whether geometric alignment corresponds to transferable physical information. Its results refine the claim: alignment is widespread but does not generally increase with depth or model size and does not imply scientific interchangeability.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s measured alignment, scaling, metric-dependence, common-space retrieval, and physical-transfer results. The paper’s background citations and values used only to select stages or settings are not recorded as results. Aggregate rows are used where the paper reports results across all models or comparisons rather than per-model values.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether cross-survey alignment of 36 pretrained models rises with parameter count, how it depends on the similarity metric, and whether it carries transferable physical information. It argues for a restricted reading of the Platonic hypothesis, so T5 fits. Caveat: every comparison applies one model to two observational views of the same objects (HSC versus another survey; DESI uses a fixed spectral encoder). It never compares independently trained models on the same input, so its bearing on V1 is by analogy (cross-view alignment versus scale).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors support only a restricted PRH: the same model applied to different surveys recovers shared object geometry, but not a survey-invariant linear encoding of the physical properties tested. Alignment does not rise systematically with depth or parameter count. They call it a useful label-free diagnostic that is insufficient for choosing stages for cross-survey linear inference.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses layerwise cross-survey MKNN, CKA, Procrustes, retrieval, scale regressions, and physical-transfer probes on pretrained astronomy models. It is not a replication of the original PRH method; it tests a related claim in a new scientific domain with different measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth trends depend on metric: JWST exact-object MRR generally rises while MKNN, CKA, and Procrustes decline; COSMOS-Web fractions increasing are 81%, 58%, 35%, and 29% respectively. Removing leading PCs increases MKNN while reducing global metrics; small isotropic perturbations leave CKA near one but reduce MKNN to approximately 0.70. Random projection and nuisance regression have distinct effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Geometric alignment does not select or predict physically useful representations. Geometry-selected stages lose R² in all 8 comparisons (0.060–3.62). MKNN does not predict transfer for any of the 5 targets (redshift p=0.294). Figure 2 Spearman ρ ranges from −0.12 to 0.62.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model or cross-view representational similarity scores do not track shared decodable task information.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-view alignment is significant in all 139 comparisons but does not increase with depth. Early-to-late contrast is about zero (COSMOS-Web) or negative (DESI, JWST, Legacy), and peaks are often intermediate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment peaks at intermediate depth rather than rising toward output layers.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 (40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, as stated in the paper)
record.problems: The study covers one scientific domain and uses HSC as the common reference; it evaluates fixed pretrained representations and unchanged linear ridge probes for a limited set of catalog targets. The paper notes that labels carry uncertainty and survey systematics, the JWST dataset is smaller and has less statistical power, and architecture, objective, scale, and pretraining data are correlated. It does not test nonlinear adapters, all physical quantities, or causally establish why geometry is shared. Several aggregate depth contrasts are described without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Results for alternative k values are mentioned as sensitivity analyses in a released artifact but are not numerically stated in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Alignment between independently trained models on the same input (only cross-view alignment of each model is measured); capability or performance as a predictor; growth of alignment within one model family as it scales.
Entire version: no vision–language image–caption pairs.
Fitted linear maps evaluated on physical targets; stitching; relative representations; unpaired mapping.
Entire version: no feature, neuron or SAE analysis.
Neighbour count k (k=5–100 computed but not reported); out-of-distribution inputs.
Causal attribution of alignment to shared data or objectives versus a common world model (Table 7b is descriptive and confounded).

missing.what: Training-category contrasts in maximum alignment. Astronomy-specific training data: −0.0214 [−0.0270, −0.0148]. Masked reconstruction: −0.0237. Supervised images: +0.0098. These bear on whether data or objective drives alignment.
Block-update alignment: 46 of 139 update maxima exceed every saved-stage maximum; updates peak earlier in 71% of curves.
Leave-one-family-out stability: the scale model improves 11/11 families for magnitude outcomes; redshift model MSE ratio 0.976.
Cross-stage maxima: 63 of 103 maps peak on the same-index diagonal (34/36 Legacy, 14/36 JWST, 15/31 COSMOS-Web).
CKA, Procrustes and MRR values for each Table 6 control. Rows record only MKNN.

record.verdict_notes: Key caveat for V1: alignment is between views (HSC versus other survey), not between independently trained models on identical inputs, so the scale null is an analogue of PRH. Reader's V7 links on the depth rows and its V4 'challenges' from probe-transfer regressions were reassigned. The shuffle and Gaussian rows are negative controls validating MKNN, not V6 evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Tests association with parameter count and depth in the sampled pretrained models, but not whether capability growth itself predicts alignment or whether independently trained models across arbitrary architectures, objectives, and data converge as they become more capable.
No paired image-caption vision/language alignment study or analysis of alignment rising with both models’ performance.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations or analysis of shared features/subspaces across seeds.
Tests fitted linear PCA–CCA retrieval and unchanged linear-probe transfer, but not stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or other mapping procedures.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Tests differences among several similarity measures and selected transformations of the inputs. Sensitivity results for the alternative k values are said to be in the released artifact but are not reported numerically in this text; there is no explicit out-of-distribution test.

Tests incompleteness of physical transfer and lack of systematic scale/depth increases. It does not establish whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause the observed geometry.

rows.value: Every final model pair has significant local alignment; within-survey redshift prediction has mean R² = 0.503.
rows.uncertainty: Alignment significance Holm-corrected across 31 pairs; uncertainty for mean not stated.
rows.locator: Section 4; Figure 3b; Appendix A.2 and A.5

rows.subject: 31 final HSC–COSMOS-Web model pairs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Applied linear ridge probes fitted in one survey to the other survey without refitting.

conditions.value: cross-survey, both directions pooled as reported

rows.measure: Cross-survey redshift R²
rows.value: Every cross-survey transfer is negative; median R² = −1.43 and mean R² = −2.98.
rows.note: Negative R² in every pair contrasts with significant geometric alignment.
rows.check: For V4 this is an identity-map (unchanged probe) test, not a fitted linear map, so it bears only on interchangeability without any mapping. For V7 it is evidence of incomplete alignment: every one of the 31 transfers has negative R² (median −1.43).

source_check.correct: E8 calculates one R² per model and direction by pooling residual sums of squares and target moments across five held-out folds. Every cross-survey transfer is negative; median R² = −1.43; mean R² = −2.98; within-survey mean R² = 0.503. Unchanged-probe transfer is absent. These scores alone cannot determine low-loss interchangeability after a fitted map or the degree and causes of geometric convergence in V7.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Figure 3b; Appendix A.6, E8; Appendix C
source_check.problem: Directions are evaluated separately; failed unchanged probes do not establish either fitted-map failure or incomplete geometric convergence.
